title: Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons
summary: This continuation of elliptic modularity over ℚ states no mathematics of its own. Its six layers name the effective residual comparisons of the modular method: Kraus's thresholds and Martin's sharp weight-two newspace bound, the exponent bound at a removed multiplicative prime, Kraus's comparison curves of exact residual conductor with full rational two-torsion, uniform irreducibility for curves with rational two-torsion, and Lemos's surjectivity theorem for curves without complex multiplication that have a rational cyclic isogeny. These targets are planned, declaration by declaration, in the roadmap EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons, which has the same title and extends the same parent; the layers here import its declarations and plan nothing again. One input of the last layer, Chen's isogeny theorem for Cartan modular curves, is a declaration of neither roadmap: the owner records it as a gap.
readme:
The definitive document is research/blueprint/readmes/EllipticCurveModularityPartII.md.

**Purpose.** Elliptic modularity over ℚ gives a weight-two newform for every elliptic curve. The modular method needs the effective statements that follow it: how large a residual characteristic can be when a multiplicative prime leaves the level, when the newform at the residual conductor is rational, when the comparison curve keeps full rational two-torsion, and when the residual representation is irreducible or surjective uniformly in the curve.

**Scope.** None of this is planned here. It is planned in `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, a roadmap with the same title and the same parent, in its layers EC.0 to EC.5; one input of the last layer, Chen's isogeny theorem, is recorded there as a gap. The six layers of this roadmap are an index into that plan: each names its targets and the declarations that own them.

**Conventions.** Those of the owner: μ(N) is the index of Γ₀(N) in SL₂(ℤ); g⁺(N) is the dimension of the weight-two newspace of Γ₀(N) with trivial character; N(E[ℓ]) is the prime-to-ℓ Artin conductor; M₀ is the deletion level of SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6, a different number in general; a curve has no complex multiplication when its endomorphism ring over an algebraic closure is ℤ.

**Layers.** EC.1 thresholds and Martin's bound (owner EC.0, EC.2); EC.2 the removed-prime bound (owner EC.1, with one norm estimate in EC.3); EC.3 and EC.4 Kraus's two realization theorems (owner EC.3); EC.5 uniform irreducibility with two-torsion (owner EC.4, with one statement in EC.5); EC.6 Lemos's theorem (owner EC.5).

**Non-goals.** No definition, theorem, API item, unit test or planet belongs to this roadmap. The packet proposes merging it into `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`.

stages.title: Thresholds and sharp newspace dimensions
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names Kraus's thresholds F, G and H and Martin's bound 12·g⁺(N) ≤ N + 1. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here.

- Kraus's rationality threshold F: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.2/kraus-f`.
- Kraus's two-torsion threshold G: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.2/kraus-g`.
- Kraus's comparison threshold H: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.2/kraus-h`.
- Martin's sharp weight-two newspace bound: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.0/martin-bound`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.0/dimension-comparison`.

stages.title: Removed-prime exponent bounds
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names the bound ℓ ≤ (√p + 1)^((M₀+1)/6) at a removed multiplicative prime, and the norm inequalities it rests on. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here.

- The norm bound behind a congruence: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/prime-divides-integral-norm`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/trace-norm`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/bounded-integer-trace-norm`.
- The removed-prime exponent bound: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/removed-prime-bound`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/removed-prime-degree-bound`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/coefficient-orbit-degree`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/real-exponent-bound`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.1/trace-gap`.

stages.title: Rationality and exact-conductor realization
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names Kraus's Théorème 3: above F(N) the weight-two newform at the exact residual conductor is rational and gives a comparison curve of conductor N. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here.

- Rationality from finitely many prime coefficients: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/rationality-from-small-primes`.
- Integrality of the small prime coefficients above F(N): `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/rational-coefficient-forcing`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/exact-weight-two-lift`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/nonrational-witness`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/small-prime-below-f`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/bounded-integer-trace-norm`.
- The elliptic curve of a rational newform: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/rational-form-elliptic-realization`.
- Kraus's rational comparison theorem: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/kraus-rational-realization`.

stages.title: Full rational two-torsion realization
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names Kraus's Théorème 4: above H(N) the comparison curve can be taken with full rational two-torsion; and the passage from the deletion level M₀ to the residual conductor. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here.

- Finite recognition of point counts modulo four: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/finite-four-count-witness`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/prime-power-ideal-sturm`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/filtered-coefficients`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/odd-eisenstein-series`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/local-mod-four-filters`.
- Transfer of the point counts to the comparison curve: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/mod-four-trace-transfer`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/small-prime-below-g`.
- Repair of rational two-torsion by a two-isogeny: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/four-count-rational-two`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/four-count-square-classes`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/four-count-full-two-selection`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/kraus-full-two-realization`.
- Kraus's full two-torsion realization: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/kraus-full-two-realization`.
- From the deletion level to the residual conductor: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/deletion-conductor-away`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.3/deletion-level-exact-adapter`.

stages.title: Uniform two-torsion irreducibility
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names Mazur's theorem, the degrees of rational cyclic isogenies, and irreducibility of E[ℓ] for ℓ ≥ 7 with full rational two-torsion and for ℓ ≥ 11 with a rational point of order two. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here.

- Mazur's theorem on isogenies of prime degree: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/mazur-prime-isogeny-classification`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/large-prime-isogeny-cm`.
- No cyclic isogenies of degree 2ℓ or 4ℓ: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/mazur-kenku-cyclic-degrees`.
- From two-torsion and an invariant line to a cyclic isogeny: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/rational-two-times-prime`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/full-two-cyclic-four`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/full-two-times-prime`.
- Irreducibility with full rational two-torsion: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/irreducible-full-two`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/odd-irreducible-implies-absolutely-irreducible`.
- Irreducibility with a rational point of order two: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.4/irreducible-one-two`, `ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.4/odd-irreducible-implies-absolutely-irreducible`.

stages.title: Rational-isogeny uniformity
stages.description:
**Import only.** This layer names Lemos's theorem that a curve without complex multiplication and with a rational cyclic isogeny has surjective mod-p representation for every p > 37, with the integrality of j, the winding quotient and the finite lists of j-values it rests on. Every target is a declaration of `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons`, or follows from the declarations listed, and nothing is planned here. One input of this layer is a declaration of no roadmap: Chen's theorem that the Cartan correspondence induces an isogeny on the p-new quotient. `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons` uses it, records it in its gap on Chen's isogeny and the winding quotient, and assigns it to a continuation of ModularCurvesPartII; it is general theory of modular curves and is not planned here either.

- Potential good reduction under a nonsplit Cartan image: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/nonsplit-potential-multiplicative`.
- The Cartan correspondence and Chen's isogeny: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/cartan-correspondence-kills-old`.
- The winding quotient of rank zero: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/finite-winding-quotient`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/winding-period-component`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/winding-class-nonzero`.
- Formal immersion at a cusp, and the torsion image of a rational point: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/cartan-cusp-formal-immersion`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/cartan-point-torsion`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/cartan-cusp-residue`.
- Integrality of j away from p: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/cartan-denominator-exclusion`.
- Integrality of j: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/integral-j-forcing`.
- Integral j-values at the five genus-zero levels: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/genus-zero-j-numerators`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/genus-zero-j-map`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/integral-parameter-divisibility`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/finite-integral-j`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/integral-j-characterisation`.
- A proper image for p > 37 is of nonsplit Cartan type: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/proper-image-nonsplit`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/exceptional-projective-exclusion`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/projective-inertia-order`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/split-cartan-exclusion`.
- Surjectivity is a property of the j-invariant: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/quadratic-twist-surjectivity`.
- Surjectivity at the finitely many rational j-values: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/large-isogeny-j-table`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/large-isogeny-image-certificates`, `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/small-isogeny-image-certificates`.
- Lemos's theorem: `EllipticModularityEffectiveComparisons:EC.5/lemos-surjectivity`.
